issues.legal_issue: A statutory proviso restoring tenancy rights protects a tenant in a pending possession suit even when an intervening amendment had removed those rights before the restoring proviso was enacted.
material_facts: The land was held for agricultural purposes by the tenant and his predecessor from 1939, and the tenancy continued from year to year.
The tenant acquired rights under the 1948 tenancy legislation, including protection against termination and recovery of possession except in the prescribed manner.
A 1952 amendment excluded the municipal area containing the land from the operation of the 1948 legislation, after which the landlord gave notice terminating the tenancy and filed a possession suit.
A 1956 amendment introduced a proviso preserving rights acquired under the 1948 legislation despite the 1952 amendment; the possession suit was still pending when the 1956 amendment took effect.
The land did not fall within the categories excluded by the 1956 amendments.
issues.conclusion: The proviso preserved the tenant’s rights despite the 1952 exclusion, and the tenant could rely on those rights in the possession suit because it was still pending when the proviso took effect.
issues.legal_principle: A proviso ordinarily excepts or qualifies the substantive clause, but its meaning depends on interpretation and it may operate as an independent substantive provision when it addresses a matter unrelated to the main clause. The proviso here expressly preserved rights acquired under the principal tenancy legislation from the effect of the 1952 amendment, retrospectively; those rights could be asserted in a suit not finally disposed of. Section 89(2) of the tenancy legislation did not apply because it concerned rights and proceedings predating commencement of that principal legislation. Section 7 of the Bombay General Clauses Act did not defeat the express contrary intention in the proviso. The Court approved Patel Maganbhai Jethabhai v. Somabhai Sursang.

rule.if: pending_civil_possession_suit and tenant_rights_previously_acquired and intervening_law_removed_tenant_protection and restoring_law_took_effect_before_final_disposition

predicates.pending_civil_possession_suit: A landlord brought a civil suit seeking possession of land held by a tenant, and the suit remained pending when the later restoring law took effect.
predicates.tenant_rights_previously_acquired: A tenant had acquired rights under tenancy legislation before those rights were removed by a later change in the law.
predicates.intervening_law_removed_tenant_protectio: A later change in the law removed the statutory protection that had applied to the tenant or the land.
predicates.restoring_law_took_effect_before_final_d: A subsequent law restored the previously acquired rights before the possession suit was finally disposed of.

issues.definition: When a civil possession suit is pending, the tenant previously acquired rights, an intervening law removed the protection, and a restoring law took effect before final disposition, those previously acquired tenant rights remain available.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court hearing a properly instituted possession suit must refer tenancy issues assigned to a special revenue forum to that forum and then decide the suit in light of its determination, rather than dismissing the suit for want of jurisdiction.
material_facts: The landlord properly instituted a civil suit for possession and mesne profits.
The tenant relied on statutory tenancy protection, raising issues concerning whether the tenancy subsisted and whether it had been validly determined.

The tenancy legislation assigned the determination of whether a person was a tenant or protected tenant to the Mamlatdar and excluded civil-court jurisdiction over questions assigned to the statutory authorities.
A later amendment provided that when an issue assigned to a competent authority arose in a civil suit, the civil court had to stay the suit and refer the issue to that authority.
The District Judge dismissed the suit instead of referring the tenancy issues for determination.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal could not stand. The civil court had to refer the tenancy issues to the Mamlatdar as a revenue court and thereafter dispose of the suit consistently with that determination.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 70 and 85 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, questions assigned to the Mamlatdar, including whether a person is a tenant or protected tenant, are outside the civil court’s authority to decide. Section 85A requires a civil court in a properly instituted suit to stay proceedings and refer such issues to the competent authority, then dispose of the suit in accordance with that authority’s decision. The Court agreed with Pandurang Hari v. Shanker Maruti and Kalicharan Bhajanlal Bhayya v. Bai Mahalaxmi that a properly instituted suit should not be dismissed merely because tenant rights were restored, but rejected their view that the civil court could decide the issues assigned to the revenue court.

rule.if: civil_possession_suit and suit_properly_instituted and tenancy_issue_arose and issue_assigned_to_special_forum and referral_procedure_applies

predicates.civil_possession_suit: A landlord brought a civil suit seeking possession of land occupied by a tenant.
predicates.suit_properly_instituted: The civil suit was properly brought in the civil court when it was instituted.
predicates.tenancy_issue_arose: The tenant’s claim raised an issue about tenancy status or the determination of the tenancy.
predicates.issue_assigned_to_special_forum: The governing law assigned that tenancy issue to a designated authority rather than the civil court.
predicates.referral_procedure_applies: A procedure requiring the civil court to refer assigned issues to the designated authority applied to the suit.

issues.definition: When a properly instituted civil possession suit raises a tenancy issue assigned to a special forum and the referral procedure applies, the issue must be referred and the civil suit must continue for decision in light of the forum’s determination.
